questions.question: A host needs to retrieve a stable architecture note by URI. Which MCP primitive fits best?
questions.explanation: A resource exposes addressable content through a URI. A tool performs an operation, while sessions and cancellation do not model readable content.

questions.question: What should a 2026-07-28 server return when resources/read receives an unknown resource URI?
questions.explanation: The current Resources contract uses invalid parameters, code -32602, for an invalid or unknown resource URI. Empty success would hide a caller error.

questions.question: Which cache policy is safest for a user-owned note returned by resources/read?
options: Public because the URI is stable
Shared across users when the MIME type matches
questions.explanation: A user-owned result should not cross identity boundaries. A bounded private cache can reduce repeated reads while preserving the authorization context.

questions.question: What identifies every notification on a subscriptions/listen response stream?
options: The original listen request ID in subscription metadata
questions.explanation: The JSON-RPC ID of subscriptions/listen becomes io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId and is repeated in the acknowledgment and every later event.

questions.question: Why must resources/list and prompts/list be deterministic for the same request inputs?
options: To grant public access to all returned entries
To stabilize caches, snapshots, and host interfaces
To make list membership depend on a prior read
questions.explanation: Stable membership and ordering prevent noisy cache misses and changing interfaces. Authorization can still affect visibility because credentials are explicit request input.

questions.question: What must a current MCP server expose even when clients may call resources/list directly?
options: A resources/subscribe method for every URI
An initialize method that creates a protocol session
A standalone HTTP GET event stream
server/discover with supported revisions and capabilities
questions.explanation: Servers must implement server/discover so clients can obtain one capability and version snapshot. Calling it remains optional for a client, which may call another method and handle a structured version error.
